preamble: Assibilation of the palatalized velar [kʲ] to the alveolar fricative [s] is the classic satem outcome of the Proto-Indo-European palatovelar *ḱ, conventionally interpreted as a palatalized velar. Armenian shows *ḱ > s directly (*ḱḗrdi- > sirt 'heart', *déḱm̥ > tasn 'ten'), and Slavic has s in the same words (*ḱm̥tóm > OCS съто, Russian сто 'hundred'), where Balto-Slavic is usually reconstructed with an intermediate *ś on the evidence of Lithuanian š.

examples.note: Proto-Balto-Slavic is reconstructed as *śímtan, with the sibilant *ś inferred from Lithuanian šimtas; no such stage is documented on the Slavic line.

sources: Kortlandt, F. (1994). From Proto-Indo-European to Slavic. Journal of Indo-European Studies, 22, 91–112. https://www.kortlandt.nl/publications/art066e.pdf
